text:
Roman Kantserov was the first NHL rookie to reach 10 goals this season, and he kept going: a hat trick and an assist in Sunday's 6-3 win in Vancouver put him at 13 goals in 24 games. Chicago took him 44th overall in 2023, and he arrived after 36 goals in 63 KHL games for Metallurg Magnitogorsk. Forwards picked in that range typically score about 0.30 points a game in their first real NHL season. He's at 0.75. The Athletic's Mark Lazerus summed him up: "He's 5-9, but plays like a power forward in tight."

Now the honest part. He's shooting 30% on 6.3 expected goals (the quality of his chances), a finishing rate that rarely lasts, and Chicago has been outchanced with him on at five on five, taking 42% of the expected goals. A power play that Lazerus noted has gone 10-for-17 over six games has helped as well. Our numbers still project about 30 goals, which keeps him firmly in the rookie-of-the-year conversation. Watch his five-on-five chances as the shooting percentage settles.
headline: Roman Kantserov keeps scoring, and the Calder talk grows
